items.stem: A process produces 70,000 defects per million opportunities. Using the Z table and the 1.5σ shift convention, what is its sigma level?
items.explanation: Tail area 0.070000 gives a long-term Z of 1.48. Sigma level = 1.48 + 1.5 = 2.98σ.

items.stem: Which of the five S's does this represent? Area audits are scored weekly and reviewed by the plant manager.
items.explanation: Self-Discipline. Audits and habit-building sustain the gains.

items.stem: Which cost-of-quality category is this? The cost of an FMEA workshop before a launch.
items.explanation: Prevention. Planning and FMEA are prevention costs.

items.stem: Which waste (IASSC wording) does this describe? A warehouse keeps eight months of stock of a slow-moving part.
items.explanation: Inventory. More material than needed is inventory.

items.stem: An audit of 200 units, each with 5 opportunities for a defect, finds 41 defects. What is the DPMO?
A process adds 12 minutes of value inside a total lead time of 2 hours. What is the process cycle efficiency?
Which of the five S's does this represent? A one-page photo standard is posted at every cell.
items.explanation: Standardize. Posted rules and visual standards are Standardize.

items.stem: A process has three steps with first-time yields of 0.95, 0.97, and 0.99. What is the rolled throughput yield?
items.explanation: RTY = 0.95 × 0.97 × 0.99 = 0.9123, or 91.2%. It is always at or below the lowest step yield.

items.stem: Which cost-of-quality category is this? The cost of reworking units that failed final test.
items.explanation: Internal failure. The defect was found before the customer received it.

items.stem: A project needs a $45,000 investment and saves $40,000 per year. What is the payback period in years?
Which Lean term does this describe? Smoothing the mix and volume of production across the day.
Which role does this describe? Removes an organizational roadblock between two departments.
A 480-minute shift includes 30 minutes of breaks, and demand is 80 units per shift. What is the takt time in minutes per unit?
items.explanation: Available time = 480 − 30 = 450 minutes. Takt = 450 ÷ 80 = 5.62 minutes per unit.

items.stem: Which Lean term does this describe? Cutting a changeover from 90 minutes to 12 minutes.
A project costs $30,000 and delivers $60,000 in benefits. What is the ROI?
Which cost-of-quality category is this? The cost of handling warranty claims.
items.explanation: External failure. Warranty costs arise after the customer has the product.

items.stem: Which waste (IASSC wording) does this describe? Two systems require the same customer data to be keyed in separately.
items.explanation: Overprocessing. Duplicate entry is extra processing that adds no value.

items.stem: Which waste (IASSC wording) does this describe? Bad solder joints are reworked at a repair bench.
items.explanation: Correction. Redoing work because something went wrong is correction.

items.stem: Which waste (IASSC wording) does this describe? A supervisor asks for a daily report in four formats, and only one is ever read.
items.explanation: Overprocessing. Doing more work than the customer values is overprocessing.

items.stem: A process has 75 orders in progress and completes 10 orders per day. What is the average lead time in days?
items.explanation: Little's Law: lead time = WIP ÷ throughput = 75 ÷ 10 = 7.50 days.

items.stem: Which measurement system error does this describe? A scale was correct in March but reads 3 grams high by September.
items.explanation: Stability. Bias that changes over time is stability.

items.stem: A team adds an automatic check at a station that will catch a defect before it leaves. Which FMEA rating should improve?
items.explanation: A better detection control lowers the Detection rating.

items.stem: What type of data is this? Whether a weld passes or fails.
Two independent parts are stacked. Their standard deviations are 3 and 4. What is the standard deviation of the stack?
In a C&E matrix the output importances are 8 and 5. An input is rated 1 against the first output and 9 against the second. What is its score?
A stable process has mean 108, within-subgroup standard deviation 4, USL = 130, and LSL = 70. What is Cpk?
items.explanation: Cpu = 1.83, Cpl = 3.17. Cpk is the smaller, 1.83. (Cp would be 2.50.)

items.stem: Which graph is best for this purpose? See whether temperature is related to the defect rate.
items.explanation: Scatterplot. Two continuous variables call for a scatterplot.

items.stem: Which measurement system error does this describe? The gage average differs from the master by the same amount across the whole range.
items.explanation: Bias. A constant offset from the reference is bias.

items.stem: In an attribute agreement study the observed agreement is 0.94 and the agreement expected by chance is 0.6. What is kappa?
A value stream map shows three processing steps of 12, 5, and 8 minutes, with a total of 4 hours of waiting. Assuming all processing is value-added, what is the process cycle efficiency?
A process is normal with mean 100 and standard deviation 4. What percent of output exceeds 108?
A master part is certified at 25.00. A gage's average reading on it is 25.04. What is the bias?
Which measurement system error does this describe? A master part reads 0.05 high every time it is measured.
items.explanation: Bias. Average reading minus the reference is bias.

items.stem: A stable process has Cpk = 1.67. What is its approximate short-term sigma level?
Which type of FMEA analyzes a product design?
items.explanation: DFMEA is design, and PFMEA is process.

items.stem: What type of data is this? A customer rating from 1 to 5.
A sample has the values 26, 11, 19, 13, 9. What is the sample standard deviation?
A Gage R&R study has GRR SD = 0.050 and part-to-part SD = 0.4. What is the number of distinct categories (software truncates the result)?
A Gage R&R study gives repeatability SD = 0.03, reproducibility SD = 0.03, and part-to-part SD = 0.8. What is %Study Variation?
A failure mode has Severity 7, Occurrence 7, and Detection 6. What is its RPN?
Which hypothesis test fits? Mean weights from three suppliers are compared, with normal data.
items.explanation: One-way ANOVA. Three groups of normal data.

items.stem: Two samples give defective rates of 15% (n = 200) and 8% (n = 200). Using the Reference Document's unpooled form, what is the z statistic?
How many observations are needed to estimate a mean to within ±3 at 95% confidence if σ = 10?
Which hypothesis test fits? A team asks whether defect type depends on supplier, using counts.
items.explanation: Chi-square contingency test. Counts classified by two categorical variables.

items.stem: A process has σ = 12. What is the standard error of the mean for samples of n = 64?
Which describes this situation? A test correctly rejects a null hypothesis that is false.
items.explanation: A correct decision. Rejecting a false null is correct, and its probability is the power.

items.stem: A sample of 16 has a mean of 60 and a standard deviation of 6. What is the upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the mean?
A sample of 9 has mean 104 and standard deviation 6. What is the 1-sample t statistic for H0: μ = 100?
Defects occur at an average of 3 per unit. What is the probability a unit has exactly 1 defects?
25 operators are measured before and after training. The mean difference is 1.0 and the standard deviation of the differences is 4. What is the paired t statistic?
In a contingency table a cell has row total 40, column total 70, and grand total 200. What is the expected count?
Which distribution models this? The time between calls arriving at a steady average rate.
items.explanation: Exponential. Time between random events is exponential.

items.stem: Which describes this situation? A test fails to reject a null hypothesis that is true.
items.explanation: A correct decision. Failing to reject a true null is correct.

items.stem: In an ANOVA, SS between = 90 with 3 df, and SS within = 90 with 12 df. What is F?
Which hypothesis test fits? A skewed sample that cannot be assumed symmetric is compared with a target median of 30.
items.explanation: 1-sample sign test. No symmetry assumption is needed for the sign test.

items.stem: Which hypothesis test fits? Three groups have extreme outliers, and a robust comparison of medians is wanted.
items.explanation: Mood's median test. Mood's median is robust to outliers.

items.stem: Which distribution models this? The time to failure of parts that wear out, with an increasing failure rate.
items.explanation: Weibull. Weibull models failure behavior; a shape above 1 means wear-out.

items.stem: Which hypothesis test fits? Rejects before and after a change are 14 of 400 and 6 of 400.
Which hypothesis test fits? Eight judges each rank the same five designs, and ratings are not normal.
items.explanation: Friedman test. Every judge rates every design, so judge is the block.

items.stem: A process has a 20% defective rate. In a sample of 8, what is the probability of exactly 2 defective?
True or False: The p-value for a regression slope tests whether the slope equals zero.
A model with n = 40 observations and k = 3 predictors has R² = 0.8. What is the adjusted R²?
What does this residual pattern indicate? Residuals are positive, then negative, then positive across the range of X.
items.explanation: Wrong functional form (curved). Sign patterns across X indicate curvature.

items.stem: What does this residual pattern indicate? Residuals form long runs of the same sign when plotted in time order.
items.explanation: Dependence over time. Runs versus order suggest dependence.

items.stem: What does this residual pattern indicate? Residuals versus fits show random scatter around zero with no pattern.
items.explanation: No problem. A random scatter supports the model assumptions.

items.stem: Which interval should be used to describe the next single unit at a given X?
items.explanation: A single future value needs the wider prediction interval.

items.stem: Regressing one predictor on the others gives R² = 0.9. What is its VIF?
Adding a predictor raises R² from 0.80 to 0.81, but adjusted R² falls. What is the best conclusion?

options.html: The added term is probably not useful
The added term is very useful

items.explanation: Adjusted R² penalizes terms that do not help.

items.stem: A simple regression with n = 12 has SST = 200 and SSE = 60. What is F?
A model has a high overall F and R², but none of the individual predictors is significant. What is the likely cause?
True or False: Box-Cox requires strictly positive data.
items.explanation: Add a constant first if there are zeros or negatives.

items.stem: For a data set, Sxy = 48, Sxx = 50, and Syy = 60. What is the correlation coefficient r?
True or False: A correlation near 0 proves there is no relationship of any kind.
A Box-Cox analysis gives a 95% confidence interval for λ of 0.7 to 1.4. What should the team do?

options.html: Use no transformation, because the interval contains 1

items.explanation: If the interval contains 1, no transformation may be needed.

items.stem: True or False: A VIF above 5 is a rule-of-thumb warning of multicollinearity.
A correlation of r = -0.6 is found between two variables. What is the coefficient of determination r²?
A regression slope is 1.5 with a standard error of 0.5. What is the t statistic for H0: slope = 0?
A fitted line is Ŷ = 10 + 2X. What is the predicted value at X = 4?
What does this residual pattern indicate? Residual spread shrinks as the fitted values grow.
items.explanation: Non-constant variance. A narrowing funnel is also non-constant variance.

items.stem: An observed value is 20 and the fitted value is 10.4. What is the residual?
An individuals chart has X̄ = 20 and an average moving range of 2. Using the n = 2 constants (d2 = 1.128), what is the UCL of the individuals chart?
An Xbar-S chart uses subgroups of n = 5, with S̄ = 2. What is the UCL of the S chart?
Using the standardized CuSum Sₙ = (1 ÷ σ) × Σ(xᵢ − T), a process has T = 100, σ = 2, and four readings 102, 101, 102, 99. What is S₄?
How is this device classified? A machine will not start until its guard is closed.
items.explanation: Prevention (control) type. An interlock prevents the error.

items.stem: A control chart is stable, but 4% of parts are out of specification. What is the best response?

options.html: Improve the process itself by reducing variation or recentering

items.explanation: A stable but incapable process needs a change to the process.

items.stem: A p chart has p̄ = 0.05 and an average subgroup size of 100. What is the upper control limit?
How is this device classified? A light flashes if a screw is missing from a tray, and work continues.
items.explanation: Warning (detection) type. It warns but does not block the next step.

items.stem: Which control chart fits? The number of defects is counted on identical circuit boards.
items.explanation: c chart. Defect counts with a constant area use a c chart.

items.stem: An EWMA chart uses λ = 0.3 and a starting value (EWMA₀) of 50. The first reading is 58. What is EWMA₁?
A c chart tracks defects on identical units with an average of 36 defects per unit. What is the upper control limit?
Which control chart fits? A team wants to detect a small, sustained drift in the mean quickly.
items.explanation: CuSum or EWMA. These charts accumulate small shifts.

items.stem: An np chart uses samples of n = 100, and the average defective rate is p̄ = 0.05. What is the lower control limit?
items.explanation: np̄ = 5. The computed lower limit is -1.54, which is negative, so it is set to 0.

items.stem: An Xbar-S chart uses subgroups of n = 8, with X̿ = 100 and S̄ = 4. What is the UCL of the Xbar chart?
An Xbar-R chart uses subgroups of n = 3, with X̿ = 50 and R̄ = 10. Using the constants table, what is the UCL of the Xbar chart?
An Xbar-R chart uses subgroups of n = 4, with R̄ = 4. What is the UCL of the R chart?
A u chart has ū = 1.2 defects per unit and an average subgroup size of 20. What is the upper control limit?
Demand is 150 units per hour, the replenishment lead time is 20 minutes, the safety factor is 25%, and each container holds 8 units. How many kanbans are needed?
Which is the correct order of actions after a special-cause signal?
items.explanation: Contain first so suspect product does not reach the customer.

items.stem: Which control chart fits? Defects per invoice are tracked where the invoice length varies.
items.explanation: u chart. Defect counts with varying size use a u chart.

items.stem: Which control chart fits? Defective units are counted out of exactly 150 inspected each day.
items.explanation: np chart. Defective units with a constant sample use an np chart.
